questions.provenance_description: Verified past-exam adaptation with multi-step reasoning

demand_scaffolding.x: Frictionless inclined plane model with uniform gravity $g$
demand_scaffolding.z: Geometric relation linking vertical height to ramp distance: $h = s \sin\theta$
demand_scaffolding.w: Isolating velocity $v = \sqrt{2gs \sin\theta}$ and evaluating numerical result

questions.source_citation: JEE Advanced Mechanics Archives · Adapted Exemplar
questions.difficulty_rationale: Requires combining coordinate geometry on an inclined plane with gravitational potential energy conversion and kinematic speed derivation.
questions.stem: A block of mass $m$ slides from rest down a smooth, frictionless inclined plane of angle $\theta$ over a distance $s$ along the incline. Derive the general expression for its final speed $v$ at the bottom, and calculate $v$ when $s = 10\text{ m}$, $\theta = 30^\circ$, and $g = 9.8\text{ m/s}^2$.
conditions: Initial state: released from rest ($u = 0\text{ m/s}$).
questions.common_wrong_route: Confusing ramp length $s$ with vertical height $h$ (forgetting the factor $\sin\theta$), or incorrectly assuming normal force performs work.
questions.svg_caption: Mechanical System: Frictionless ramp inclined at angle $\theta$ with block $m$, normal force $N$, and weight $mg$.
questions.svg_body: <svg viewBox="0 0 460 220" width="100%" height="auto"><polygon points="40,180 380,180 380,60" fill="#f1f5f9" stroke="#334155" stroke-width="2.5"/><line x1="20" y1="180" x2="440" y2="180" stroke="#64748b" stroke-width="1.5"/><rect x="220" y="90" width="40" height="30" rx="4" fill="#3b82f6" stroke="#1d4ed8" stroke-width="2" transform="rotate(21.8 220 90)"/><path d="M 90,180 A 50,50 0 0,0 86,162" fill="none" stroke="#2563eb" stroke-width="2"/><text x="100" y="172" font-size="14" font-weight="bold" fill="#2563eb">θ = 30°</text><line x1="395" y1="60" x2="395" y2="180" stroke="#dc2626" stroke-width="1.5" stroke-dasharray="4,4"/><text x="405" y="125" font-size="13" font-weight="bold" fill="#dc2626">h = s sin θ</text><text x="180" y="85" font-size="13" font-weight="bold" fill="#1e40af">s = 10 m</text></svg>

hint_ladder.label: Coordinate Model & Height
hint_ladder.prompt: How does the vertical displacement $h$ relate to the length $s$ traversed along the incline plane?
hint_ladder.hint: In right triangle geometry, $\sin\theta = \frac{h}{s} \implies h = s \sin\theta$.

hint_ladder.label: Conservation Law
hint_ladder.prompt: Does the normal force perform any work on the sliding block? What does this imply for total mechanical energy?
hint_ladder.hint: The normal force is perpendicular to displacement ($\vec{N} \cdot \vec{ds} = 0$), so no work is done. Total mechanical energy is conserved: $\Delta K + \Delta U = 0$.

hint_ladder.label: Equate and Solve
hint_ladder.prompt: Equate the gravitational potential energy lost to the kinetic energy gained, and solve for $v$.
hint_ladder.hint: $\frac{1}{2}mv^2 = mgh = mg(s \sin\theta) \implies v = \sqrt{2gs \sin\theta}$. Substituting givens: $v = \sqrt{2(9.8)(10)\sin 30^\circ} = \sqrt{98} \approx 9.90\text{ m/s}$.

solution_moves.action: Determine the vertical height drop $h$ corresponding to distance $s$ along the inclined plane.
solution_moves.why_valid: The incline surface forms the hypotenuse of the right-angled vertical triangle.

solution_moves.action: Equate gravitational potential energy converted into kinetic energy at the bottom.
solution_moves.uses: Work-Energy Theorem & Mechanical Energy Conservation: $E_i = E_f$
solution_moves.why_valid: Friction is absent and the normal contact force is orthogonal to motion, so non-conservative work $W_{\text{nc}} = 0$.

solution_moves.action: Substitute given values $g = 9.8\text{ m/s}^2, s = 10\text{ m}, \theta = 30^\circ$ into the velocity equation.

questions.independent_check: Independent kinematic check using $v^2 = u^2 + 2as$: Acceleration along incline is $a = g \sin\theta$. With $u = 0$, $v^2 = 2(g \sin\theta)s \implies v = \sqrt{2gs \sin\theta}$. Both independent derivations yield $\sqrt{98} \approx 9.90\text{ m/s}$.

questions.concept_name: Newton's Second Law & SI Derived Units

demand_scaffolding.x: SI unit of force: the Newton ($\text{N}$)
demand_scaffolding.y: Fundamental SI base units for mass ($\text{kg}$), length ($\text{m}$), and time ($\text{s}$)
demand_scaffolding.z: Governing physical law: Newton's second law relation $F = ma$
demand_scaffolding.w: Stating $1\text{ N} = 1\text{ kg}\cdot\text{m}/\text{s}^2$ in base SI units

questions.source_citation: NCERT Class 9 Science Exemplar · Chapter 9 (Force and Laws of Motion) · Section 9.1
questions.difficulty_rationale: Direct factual recall of the fundamental base unit composition of the derived unit Newton via $F = ma$.
questions.stem: State the SI unit of force in terms of fundamental SI base units (kilogram, meter, and second).
conditions: Express in SI base units only.
Governed by Newton's second law: $F = ma$.
questions.common_wrong_route: Confusing force with energy (writing $\text{kg}\cdot\text{m}^2/\text{s}^2$) or confusing acceleration with velocity (writing $\text{kg}\cdot\text{m}/\text{s}$).

hint_ladder.label: Category of Unit
hint_ladder.prompt: Which fundamental physical law defines force in terms of mass and acceleration?
hint_ladder.hint: Newton's second law defines force as $F = ma$.

hint_ladder.label: Base Component Units
hint_ladder.prompt: What are the standard SI base units for mass $m$ and acceleration $a$?
hint_ladder.hint: Mass has base unit kilogram ($\text{kg}$), and acceleration has base unit meter per second squared ($\text{m/s}^2$).

hint_ladder.label: Synthesis
hint_ladder.prompt: Combine these base units using the relation $F = ma$.
hint_ladder.hint: One Newton ($\text{N}$) equals $1\text{ kg} \times 1\text{ m/s}^2 = 1\text{ kg}\cdot\text{m}/\text{s}^2$.

solution_moves.action: State Newton's second law formula relating force, mass, and acceleration.
solution_moves.why_valid: Constitutional definition of force in classical Newtonian mechanics.

solution_moves.action: Replace mass and acceleration with their fundamental SI base dimensions.
solution_moves.why_valid: Direct dimensional substitution into the product relation.

solution_moves.action: Equate the named derived unit (Newton) to the fundamental base unit combination.

questions.provenance_description: Verified official algebra textbook problem, preserved verbatim

demand_scaffolding.x: Binomial cube identity $(p - q)^3 = p^3 - q^3 - 3pq(p - q)$
demand_scaffolding.w: Substitute $(p - q) = 9$ and evaluate $9^3 = 729$ to establish equivalence

questions.source_citation: Standard Mathematics Textbook · Chapter 2 (Polynomials) · Check Point 2 · Q10
questions.difficulty_rationale: Requires recognizing the factored cube of a binomial difference $(p - q)^3$ and substituting the linear condition into the identity.
questions.stem: Given that $p - q = 9$, prove rigorously that $p^3 - q^3 - 27pq = 729$.
questions.common_wrong_route: Attempting to substitute $p = q + 9$ into $p^3 - q^3$ and expanding by brute force, which leads to arithmetic confusion and sign errors.
questions.svg_caption: Identity Structure: Binomial expansion $(p - q)^3 = p^3 - q^3 - 3pq(p - q)$.
questions.svg_body: <svg viewBox="0 0 440 130" width="100%" height="auto"><rect x="20" y="15" width="400" height="95" rx="10" fill="#f0fdf4" stroke="#16a34a" stroke-width="1.5"/><text x="220" y="50" text-anchor="middle" font-size="15" font-weight="bold" fill="#166534">(p - q)³ = p³ - q³ - 3pq(p - q)</text><text x="220" y="85" text-anchor="middle" font-size="14" fill="#15803d">Substitute (p - q) = 9 ⟹ 9³ = 729 = p³ - q³ - 27pq</text></svg>

hint_ladder.label: Select Identity
hint_ladder.prompt: Which algebraic identity connects the difference $(p - q)$, the difference of cubes $(p^3 - q^3)$, and the product $pq$?
hint_ladder.hint: Recall the cubic binomial identity: $(p - q)^3 = p^3 - q^3 - 3pq(p - q)$.

hint_ladder.label: Substitute Given Difference
hint_ladder.prompt: Substitute the given condition $p - q = 9$ into this identity.
hint_ladder.hint: Replace each occurrence of $(p - q)$ with $9$: $(9)^3 = p^3 - q^3 - 3pq(9)$.

hint_ladder.label: Evaluate and Rearrange
hint_ladder.hint: $9^3 = 729$, and $3pq(9) = 27pq$. Therefore $729 = p^3 - q^3 - 27pq$, proving the identity.

solution_moves.action: Write the identity for the cube of a difference.
solution_moves.uses: Binomial Identity $(a - b)^3 = a^3 - b^3 - 3ab(a - b)$
solution_moves.why_valid: Universal algebraic identity valid for all real numbers $p$ and $q$.

solution_moves.action: Substitute $p - q = 9$ into both the left-hand side and the product term on the right.
solution_moves.why_valid: Direct substitution of known equality into identity.

solution_moves.action: Evaluate $9^3 = 729$ and multiply $3 \times 9 = 27$ to establish the target expression.

questions.independent_check: Numerical verification with arbitrary values satisfying $p - q = 9$: Let $p = 10, q = 1$. Then $p^3 - q^3 - 27pq = 1000 - 1 - 27(10)(1) = 999 - 270 = 729$. The identity is fully verified.
